title: Rapid response message architectures and war-room checklist
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, copy-first runbook for incident communications used by SREs and Oncall to get a war-room stood up, publish a clear public status, and send coordinated customer-facing updates. Focus: clarity, cadence, safety (no speculation), and minimal but informative public messages.

Scope and when to use this doc:
- Use for any incident impacting customer-facing inference APIs, console workflows, or telemetry that persists beyond a single automatic retry (severity P2/P1).
- For short flaps (<5 minutes) that recover automatically, use a brief internal note — no public status unless customer impact seen.

Roles (quick reference):
- Incident Lead (IL): owns triage, decisions, and next-update cadence.
- Communications Lead (CL): drafts public and customer messages, coordinates with CS and legal.
- SRE Triage: initial diagnostics, mitigation attempts, and runbook execution.
- Engineering Lead: deploy/blocker decisions, rollback ownership.
- Customer Support Lead: surfaces critical customer tickets; prepares targeted customer outreach.
- Legal/Compliance: engaged if PII/security exposure suspected.

War-room quick checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Create incident channel: #war-{{INCIDENT_ID}} (private) and add IL, CL, SREs, Eng lead, CS lead.
2) Assign IL and CL explicitly in channel header.
3) Record initial timeline: detection time, first alert source, initial symptom.
4) Snapshot status page: record current public page state and any existing messages.
5) Set update cadence: default 15 minutes until degradation/mitigation then extend.
6) Start triage: identify impacted services, affected regions, topology (host vs infra vs model).
7) If customer-visible: post initial status page entry (see templates below).
8) Put a readout in #oncall-escalations: 1-line summary + link to war-room channel.
9) Create a ticket in JIRA with incident tag and link to war-room and status page.
10) Decide on targeted customer notifications (CS-led) for top-tier customers.

Status page templates (copy-first; edit variables in place):
- Status: Investigating (public short)
  Title: "Investigating service degradation affecting inference API"
  Impact: "Some requests may fail or experience increased latency in US and EU regions."
  What we know: "Beginning at {{DETECTED_AT}} we observed elevated 5xx/errors and increased tail latency for text generation endpoints."
  What we're doing: "SREs are actively investigating routing and model-serving nodes. We will post updates every 15 minutes or as significant milestones occur."
  ETA for next update: "{{NEXT_UPDATE_TIME}}"
  Affected services: "Inference API (completion/chat), streaming responses"
  Workaround: "Retrying requests with exponential backoff may succeed; we are not recommending model changes at this time."

- Status: Partial service restored (public short)
  Title: "Partial restoration: inference request success rates improving"
  Impact: "A portion of requests remain affected; a subset of traffic now routed to fallback instances."
  What we know: "Mitigation applied at {{MITIGATION_AT}}: traffic routing adjusted to fallback pool which reduced error rate by ~70%."
  What we're doing: "Monitoring to confirm stability and rolling out a permanent fix. Next update in 30 minutes."
  Workaround: "No action required from customers; continuing retries are honored."

- Status: Resolved (public short)
  Title: "Incident resolved: inference API back to expected levels"
  Impact: "All services restored to normal performance."
  What we know: "Root cause under investigation; mitigation fully restored traffic at {{RESOLVED_AT}}. A follow-up postmortem will be shared within 5 business days."
  What we're doing: "Collecting logs and KV cache states for RCA. If you continue to see problems, contact support with incident ID {{INCIDENT_ID}}."

Customer-facing message templates (email / support message):
- Initial customer alert (short):
  Subject: "Notice: Service disruption impacting Redwood inference API ({{INCIDENT_ID}})"
  Body: "Hello,

We're investigating an issue affecting inference requests that started at {{DETECTED_AT}} which may cause failed or delayed responses. Our engineers are working on a fix and we'll send updates by {{NEXT_UPDATE_TIME}}. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a full summary after resolution.

If you have a critical impact or active incident in your product, reply to this message and we'll prioritize a direct touch.

— Redwood SRE Team"

- Follow-up/update to affected customers (mid-incident):
  Subject: "Update: Ongoing investigation for {{INCIDENT_ID}} — next steps"
  Body: "Hello,

Quick update: Our mitigation reduced error rates by {{PERCENT}}%. We are continuing to monitor and apply a permanent fix. We expect the next status update at {{NEXT_UPDATE_TIME}}.

We will proactively notify you once your traffic is confirmed stable. Thanks for bearing with us.

— Redwood SRE"

- Resolution summary (short RCAs go to customers, full postmortem internal):
  Subject: "Resolved: Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — summary and next steps"
  Body: "Hello,

The incident that began at {{DETECTED_AT}} has been resolved as of {{RESOLVED_AT}}. Impact: failed or delayed inference requests for some customers in US/EU regions. Root cause: degraded routing state caused by a configuration drift in the autoscaling controller (high level). Mitigation: we rolled back the faulty config and restored traffic to healthy model-serving pools.

Actions taken: rollback at {{MITIGATION_AT}}, additional guardrail added to autoscaler, and alerting tuned to catch config drift earlier.

Next steps: we will publish a detailed postmortem in 3 business days with timeline and remediation items. If you observed persistent errors after resolution, please reply with your request IDs and region.

— Redwood SRE & Product"

Internal Slack/war-room announcement samples (concise):
- Initial ping (one-liner): "INCIDENT {{INCIDENT_ID}}: Investigating elevated 5xx on inference-api — war-room #war-{{INCIDENT_ID}}. IL=@Priya. Next update in 15m."
- Escalation ping to Director: "Escalation: Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} impacting production inference for multiple customers; IL assigned, mitigation in progress. Joining war-room: @Director-Eng."
Do / Don't list for communications lead:
Do:
- Use the template language of 'what we know / what we're doing / next update'.
- Keep public messages under 4–6 bullet lines for clarity.
- Coordinate targeted customer outreach for top-10 accounts.
- Timestamp messages and include incident ID every time.
Don't:
- Don't speculate about root cause in public messages.
- Don't promise exact ETA unless confirmed.
- Don't include internal debugging output or stack traces in public notes.

Posting cadence and escalation rules:
- Start: updates every 15 minutes for the first hour.
- If stabilization occurs: move to every 30–60 minutes until fully resolved.
- If a mitigation is in place but a long-term fix is needed: hourly updates and an ETA for postmortem.
- If incident reaches SEV0/P1 and affects >30% of traffic: exec notification and dedicated comms to top customers.

Technical steps for status page update (reference):
1) Title: short, action-oriented.
2) Set impact correctly (degraded / partial outage / major outage).
3) Use the three-part structure in the public body (what we know / what we're doing / next update).
4) Add 'affected services' list and approximate scope (regions, endpoints).
5) Add a one-line workaround when available.
6) Publish and pin latest update; remove stale workarounds if replaced.

Post-incident checklist (after resolved):
- Lock timeline and collect logs. Owner: SRE Triage.
- Communications: publish resolution and planned RCA cadence. Owner: CL.
- Customer tickets: CS to follow-up with any flagged customers and offer credits if warranted.
- Postmortem: IL to schedule RCA within 3 business days; include impact metrics and remediation owners.
- Action items: convert remediation tasks to tracked JIRA issues and assign SLAs.

Templates for postmortem public summary (short):
- Headline: "Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}}: Summary — {{SHORT_DESCRIPTION}}"
- One-paragraph timeline, one-paragraph root cause (non-technical high-level), list of remediation actions and owners, and link to full internal postmortem.

Quick reference snippets (copy-paste ready):
- "We are investigating increased error rates for inference endpoints. Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}. Next update: {{NEXT_UPDATE_TIME}}."
- "Mitigation applied: traffic reroute to fallback pool reduced errors by ~{{PERCENT}}%. Monitoring closely. Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}."
- "Resolved: service restored. We will publish a detailed postmortem by {{PM_DUE_DATE}}. If you see residual issues, include request IDs and region in replies."

Notes and rationale:
- Keep customer messages short and action-oriented; customers prefer a reliable cadence vs verbose technical detail.
- Avoid premature diagnosis; internal channels can include detailed logs, public messages should not.
- Templates should be used as-is for speed; CL can add 1–2 customer-specific lines when necessary.

Open questions / TODOs for this doc:
- Add a ready-to-send SMS/phone script for top-10 customers.
- Define explicit crediting policy text for long outages.
- Add a step-by-step UI guide to update the status.redwood.ai page for new hires.

End of runbook draft.
